hub.intro: Deep work, mock exams, classroom activities. Simple timers that run right in your browser, with no install and no account.
hub.aboutHtml:
TimerDesk is a set of focused time tools for students, teachers and anyone who needs to stay on track. Every tool is free, needs no login, and keeps your settings and history only in your own browser.

All timers support fullscreen and keep-screen-on, so they work well on a classroom TV or projector. Time is calculated from the real clock, so the countdown stays accurate even when you switch tabs.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy – TimerDesk
privacy.description: TimerDesk privacy policy. There are no accounts, and your settings and history are stored only in your browser.
privacy.html:
1. Information we collect

TimerDesk has no accounts or sign-in, and does not directly collect personal information such as your name, email address or phone number.

2. Data stored in your browser

Timer settings (durations, sounds, colors) and focus history are stored only in your device's browser storage (localStorage) and are never sent to our servers. Clearing your browser's site data removes them.

3. Advertising and cookies

To cover running costs, this site may show third-party ads such as Google AdSense. Third-party vendors, including Google, use cookies to serve ads based on your prior visits to this website or other websites. You can opt out of personalized advertising in Google Ads Settings. Learn more about how Google uses advertising cookies in Google's advertising policies.

4. Analytics

To improve the service we may use analytics tools such as Google Analytics to collect anonymous usage statistics (page views, device type). This information is not used to identify you.

5. Changes

If this policy changes, the updated version will be posted on this page with a new effective date.

pomodoro-timer.title: Pomodoro Timer – Free Online Focus Timer with Study Log
pomodoro-timer.description: Free online Pomodoro timer: 25 minutes of focus, 5-minute breaks, repeated automatically. Tracks today's focus time with a 7-day chart. Fullscreen, alarm sounds, no install.
pomodoro-timer.lead: Work in focused 25-minute sessions with short breaks in between. Press start and the timer switches between focus and break on its own while it logs your focus time.
pomodoro-timer.card: 25 min focus, 5 min break, on repeat, with a daily focus log

ui.resetConfirm: Clear all of your focus history?
ui.notifyFocusDone: Focus session done! Take a break.

sections.html:
The Pomodoro Technique is a time management method created by Francesco Cirillo in the late 1980s, when he was a university student studying with a tomato-shaped kitchen timer. Pomodoro is Italian for tomato.

The idea is simple: focus on one task for 25 minutes, then take a 5-minute break. That's one pomodoro. After four of them, take a longer 15–30 minute break. A fixed end point makes it easier to start, and a scheduled break helps you rest before you burn out.

1. Press Start to begin a 25-minute focus session. The space bar also starts and pauses.
  2. When focus time ends, an alarm sounds and a short break begins automatically.
  3. After four focus sessions you get a long break. The dots under the timer show where you are in the cycle.
  4. Every completed session is added to Focus minutes today and the 7-day chart.

Open Settings to change session lengths, the long-break interval, the alarm sound and auto-start. Your settings are remembered for next time.

• Start with 25/5. When 25 minutes starts to feel short, try 50/10.
  • Write down one task. "Finish 20 practice problems in chapter 3" beats "study math".
  • Leave your phone during breaks. Stand up, stretch or get water. One short video can easily turn a 5-minute break into 20.
  • Set a daily goal in pomodoros instead of hours. It's easier to track and easier to hit.

faq.q: Does the timer keep running if I switch tabs or minimize the window?
faq.a: Yes. Remaining time is calculated from the real end time, so it stays accurate in a background tab, and the tab title shows the time left. Closing the tab stops the timer.

faq.q: Can I change the 25-minute focus length?
faq.a: Yes. In Settings you can set focus from 1 to 180 minutes and adjust short breaks, long breaks and how often long breaks happen.

faq.q: Where is my focus history saved?
faq.a: Only in your browser's local storage. Nothing is sent to a server, so history doesn't sync across devices and is removed if you clear your browser's site data.

faq.q: Does it work on my phone?
faq.a: Yes, it works in any modern mobile or tablet browser. Where supported, the screen stays on while the timer runs.
Check that your device isn't on silent and press Test sound in Settings. Some browsers block audio until you interact with the page, so start the timer with a tap or click.

exam-timer.description: Free online exam timer for classrooms and mock tests. Build a multi-section schedule or use SAT, IELTS, TOEIC presets. Big fullscreen countdown, 10 and 5 minute warnings, current time display.
exam-timer.lead: Put a big, clear countdown on the classroom screen or run a full mock test at home. When one section ends, the timer moves on to the break and the next section automatically.
exam-timer.card: Multi-section exam countdown with SAT, IELTS and TOEIC presets

sections.h2: Built for classrooms and mock exams
sections.html:
Invigilating a classroom test

Press fullscreen and the section name and time remaining fill the screen, which makes it easy to read from the back of the room on a TV or projector. At 10 and 5 minutes left the numbers change color and an alert sounds, so you don't have to announce the time yourself.

Full-length practice tests

Choose a preset such as the Digital SAT or IELTS and the breaks between sections are built in. Practicing with real timing, including the short gaps between modules, gets you used to the pace before test day.

Your own schedule

For school midterms, finals or certification exams, edit the section names, durations and breaks in the table. Your edits are saved as a custom schedule for next time.

Timings follow each test's published format. Always confirm with the official test provider before exam day.

1. Pick a preset under Schedule, or choose Custom schedule.
  2. Edit section names, minutes and breaks in the table if needed.
  3. Set the start time. Start now begins immediately; entering a time lines the schedule up with the clock.
  4. Press Start exam, then go fullscreen (F key) for the classroom.

faq.q: Can I pause the exam timer?
faq.a: Yes. Press Pause to stop, and when you resume, the rest of the schedule shifts later by the paused time. Handy for practice sessions.
At the start of each section, 10 and 5 minutes before the end (you can turn these off in Settings), and when a section ends. The countdown turns orange at 10 minutes and red at 5 minutes.

faq.q: What happens if I enter a start time that has already passed?
faq.a: The timer jumps to whichever section should be running now. If the whole schedule would already be over, it's moved to the same time tomorrow.

faq.q: Is it accurate if I switch to another tab?
faq.a: Yes. Everything is calculated from the real clock, so the remaining time is correct when you come back.

faq.q: Can I build a schedule for my school exam?
faq.a: Add or delete sections and change names and times in the table to match any exam. Changes are saved automatically in your browser.

visual-timer.title: Visual Timer – Free Online Countdown Disc for Classrooms & Kids
visual-timer.description: Free online visual timer with a shrinking colored disc that shows time left at a glance. Drag to set, fullscreen for the classroom TV, great for kids' routines, group work and meetings.
visual-timer.lead: See time disappear instead of reading numbers. Drag the disc or tap a preset to set the time, then press start.
visual-timer.card: A shrinking colored disc shows time left, great for kids and classes

ui.dialLabel: Disc showing the time remaining. Drag to set the time.
ui.dragHint: Drag around the disc with your finger or mouse to set the time.

sections.html:
A visual timer shows time remaining as a shrinking area of color instead of numbers. Even children who can't read a clock yet understand right away that time is up when the red is gone.

Because time passing is visible at a glance, visual timers are widely used in preschool and elementary classrooms, special education and at home. They work just as well for adults keeping meetings and presentations on schedule.

• Kids' routines: 3 minutes for brushing teeth, 10 for tidying up, 30 for screen time. The disc ends the activity instead of you having to say "time's up".
  • Classroom activities: Put group work, quiz time or recess on the classroom TV so students can check the time themselves.
  • Meetings and talks: Give each speaker 5 minutes and Q&A 10 minutes to keep meetings from dragging on.
  • Focused work: If the numbers distract you, turn off Show digital time and just watch the disc.

1. Drag around the disc to set a time, or tap a preset from 1 to 60 minutes.
  2. Press Start (or the space bar) and the disc starts shrinking.
  3. When time is up, the alarm plays and the disc flashes.
  4. In Settings, change the dial range (10, 20, 30, 60 or 120 minutes), the color and the alarm sound. A 10 or 20 minute range makes short activities easier to see.

faq.q: Can I set more than 60 minutes?
faq.a: Yes. Change the Dial range to 120 minutes in Settings to set up to 2 hours.
The numbers run counterclockwise from 12 so that the edge of the disc moves clockwise, like a clock hand, as time runs out. It's the same layout used by classic classroom visual timers.

faq.q: Can I show it fullscreen on a classroom TV?
faq.a: Press the fullscreen button at the top right (or the F key) and the disc fills the screen. The screen stays on while the timer runs.

faq.q: Can I use it without sound?
faq.a: Set the volume to 0 in Settings and the disc will just flash when time is up. Good for libraries and quiet rooms.
